Why Processes Fail People

Screens

    Your industry

    Glossary

    Continuous improvement (CI)
    The ongoing practice of improving how work is done, usually in many small steps rather than a few large ones.
    Process
    Any repeatable sequence of steps that turns inputs into outputs for a customer. Covered properly in Module 2.
    Special cause
    An identifiable, non-routine source of variation — a machine fault, a bad batch of material, a power cut, a one-off event; occasionally an individual’s action. Contrasted with common cause, the ordinary variation built into how a process is designed. Deming’s 94/6 is a common-cause versus special-cause split. You work with both properly at Yellow Belt.
    Red Bead Experiment
    Deming’s classroom demonstration that individual results are driven by the system: workers scoop beads from a box that is one-fifth red, are rewarded and punished for red-bead counts they cannot control, and nothing they do changes the outcome.
    Drive out fear (Point 8)
    The eighth of Deming’s fourteen points for management. Fear stops information moving; problems that are unsafe to report cannot be fixed.
    The system
    Everything about how work is designed and managed: layout, tools, forms, software, schedules, policies, incentives, and training.
